description:
High school students across France set fires and clashed with police on Wednesday and Thursday, escalating nearly a week of disruption. As President Emmanuel Macron’s government weighs how to balance historic public debt with already strained state spending, an under-resourced, overstretched education sector lies at the root of students’ anger.

Meanwhile, nationwide protests have erupted across Spain over soaring rent, evictions, and a lack of affordable housing. The protests began after the forced eviction of an elderly woman from her apartment.

author: CNN
description:
CNN's Ed Lavandera and team spent 30 days inside a small-town hospital struggling to survive. At West River hospital in Hettinger, North Dakota, more than 13 percent of their full-time staff moved from other countries, taking jobs that, in some cases, were left open for years.

Watch the full documentary, The Whole Story with Anderson Cooper: 30 Days Inside: Hospitals and the Immigrant Workforce on Sunday, October 4 at 8pm et and streaming on CNN apps on Monday, October 5.
title: 30 days inside a hospital relying on immigrants

author: CNN
description:
President Trump's net approval rating on inflation hit -65 points in AP-NORC's cost of living poll Thursday. CNN chief data analyst Harry Enten points out that this rating is the record low not only for Trump, but for any president ever. Enten also observes that Trump is the first president to poll below -50% net approval on inflation ever: "Donald Trump is underwater. . .among Democrats, independents, and Republicans as well."

Also, Abby Phillip's "NewsNight" panel debates Trump's historic unpopularity.

1:37 "How about with independents?" Enten on implications for midterms

author: CNN
description:
52 years after his resignation and 32 years after his death, the Department of Justice is looking into whether President Richard M. Nixon was wronged by federal prosecutors investigating the Watergate scandal. Rep. Riley Moore (R-WV) said Thursday that Nixon was "absolutely couped out of office and was framed."  Moore also compared Nixon to President Donald Trump, claiming that they were both victims of the "deep state."

CNN's "NewsNight" panel debates the news, and former Nixon Library director Tim Naftali speaks with Laura Coates. Also, Jim Antle of the Washington Examiner discusses the "Nixonmaxxing" trend, in which Gen Z lionizes the ex-president.

description: In an interview with CNN, Thomas Giuffra, the lawyer for Cornell's Jane Doe, says his client "went from denial, to shame and ultimately acceptance that she had been raped by people that she thought were her friends." The DA says he did not receive all of the transcripts, while Cornell says it shared all investigative information with his office.

description:
Russian President Vladimir Putin has warned the West against escalating the war in Ukraine, saying Moscow is prepared to use “all weapons” in its arsenal — including nuclear — if its Baltic exclave of Kaliningrad comes under attack. 

Speaking at the Valdai Discussion Club in Moscow on Thursday, the Russian leader said he had no plans to attack any European country but was prepared to respond to Western aggression if necessary and referenced the Russian territory sandwiched between NATO members Poland and Lithuania. 

CNN’s Ben Hunte speaks with Paul Van Hooft, head of RAND Europe Deterrence Initiative, about Putin’s nuclear threat to NATO countries. Also, former George W. Bush national security official Meghan O’Sullivan reacts to Russia’s latest attacks in Ukraine.

author: CNN
description:
The New York Times obtained more than 1,000 pages of internal material from Cornell University's investigation into an alleged 2024 fraternity gang rape. Investigative reporter Debra Kamin revealed a moment the victim's perception of the trauma shifted after seeing an online post about the alleged assault. Reading from the leaked files, Kamin notes the survivor told investigators: “That was the first time I'd ever heard the narrative change, that I wasn't a whore and that I was assaulted.” 

The contents of the New York Times report were corroborated to CNN by Jane Doe’s attorney, who adds “we were not responsible for leaking these documents.”
title: NYT Reporter on the trove of documents that’s jolting the Cornell investigation
